schema.name: disk_drives
schema.description:
Drives with used and free space. Keywords: discos, unidades, espacio libre, cuánto queda, disk space.
Returns every mounted drive (path, label, type, total, free) plus shortcuts such as Downloads or AppData. Use it first to decide where to scan.

schema.name: disk_scan
schema.description:
Scan a folder or drive to measure what takes space. Keywords: escanear, analizar disco, qué ocupa, scan.
Walks the tree in parallel (a full 1.5 TB drive takes about a minute) and keeps a size map in memory that the other tools query. By default waits for the scan to end; with wait=false it returns at once and disk_status reports progress. Replaces any previous scan.

path.description: Absolute folder or drive to scan, e.g. C:\ or C:\Users\me

timeout_s.description: Maximum seconds to wait when wait=true

schema.name: disk_status
schema.description:
Progress of the running scan or summary of the last one. Keywords: estado, progreso, cuánto falta.
Cheap to call. Says whether a scan is running, how many files and bytes it has seen, and when done the root, total size, file and folder counts.

schema.name: disk_dir
schema.description:
Contents of a scanned folder, biggest first, with junk tags. Keywords: carpeta, qué hay dentro, listar.
Each entry has size, file count, share of the parent, last modified date and, when the catalog knows the folder, what it is and whether it is safe to delete. Files are listed live so the view is always current.

path.description: Absolute folder path, e.g. C:\Users\me or D:\. Omit for the root of the current scan.

schema.name: disk_hotspots
schema.description:
Where the space really goes: disjoint heavy spots. Keywords: puntos calientes, dónde están mis gigas.
Not a folder ranking (that repeats parent and child): a partition of the tree into pieces that do not overlap, each attributed as deep as the weight can be pinned. What is spread over many small things appears as 'scattered rest'.

schema.name: disk_junk
schema.description:
Known junk with safety level: caches, node_modules, temp. Keywords: basura, limpiar, liberar espacio.
Every item says what it is, why it is there, how it regenerates and whether it is 'safe' (regenerates alone), 'review' (heavy but recoverable) or 'danger' (never delete). Totals per category and the reclaimable sum come with it. Includes category 'Agentes de IA': caches and history of Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, Cursor, VS Code. Filter by safety, category or minimum size.

category.description: Exact category name as returned, e.g. 'Compilaciones'

schema.name: disk_stale
schema.description:
Big folders nobody touched in months. Keywords: sin tocar, olvidado, antiguo, stale, untouched.
Folders above a size floor whose newest file is older than the given number of months. Good candidates for archiving or asking the user about.

schema.name: disk_top_files
schema.description:
The heaviest single files of the scan. Keywords: ficheros grandes, archivos pesados, biggest files.
Up to 500 largest files with a note for the usual suspects (hiberfil.sys, pagefile.sys, .vhdx, Blender .blend1 copies). Optionally restrict to an extension.

schema.name: disk_types
schema.description:
Space by file category: video, AI models, archives, code. Keywords: por tipo, extensiones, file types.
Aggregates the scan by category with the top extensions of each.

schema.name: disk_find
schema.description:
Find files by name glob, extension, size or age in a folder. Keywords: buscar ficheros, mayores de, find.
Walks the folder live (bounded to max_entries) and returns matches biggest first. Combine filters: name glob (*.iso), minimum size, older than N days. Works on any folder, scanned or not.

path.description: Absolute folder path, e.g. C:\Users\me or D:\. Omit for the root of the current scan.

pattern.description: Case-insensitive glob on the file name, e.g. '*.iso' or 'backup*'

schema.name: disk_explain
schema.description:
What a folder or file is and whether it is safe to delete. Keywords: qué es esta carpeta, se puede borrar.
Matches the path against the junk catalog (node_modules, caches, WinSxS...) and the file notes, and adds its measured size when it is inside the current scan. Answers 'danger' for anything the assistant must never delete.

path.description: Absolute path of a folder or file

schema.name: disk_script
schema.description:
Write a reviewable PowerShell cleanup script for paths. Keywords: script de limpieza, powershell, dry run.
Nothing is deleted: the script is saved under the app's data folder and returned, with -WhatIf support so the user can simulate it first. Prefer this over disk_delete when the user wants to look before anything happens.

schema.name: disk_delete
schema.description:
Delete paths: Recycle Bin by default, permanent only with confirm. Keywords: borrar, eliminar, papelera.
Refuses drive roots, the profile, Windows, Program Files, 'danger' items and AI-tool config. Re-measures each item (bytes, files, newest mtime) first: if it no longer matches the scan it is NOT deleted and comes back in `changed` with hint 'rescan' (force=true skips this, only if the user insists). Returns expected_bytes (scan) vs freed_bytes (measured) and the difference; in trash mode disk space frees only when the bin is emptied.

confirm.description: Must be true for mode='permanent'. Say so to the user first.

force.description: Delete even when an item changed since the scan. Only if the user insists.

schema.name: disk_rescan
schema.description:
Re-read one subfolder and splice fresh numbers into the scan. Keywords: refrescar, actualizar, rescan.
Seconds instead of a full scan. Use it after deleting outside the app or when a folder changed.

path.description: Absolute folder path, e.g. C:\Users\me or D:\. Omit for the root of the current scan.

schema.name: disk_ollama_backups
schema.description:
Ollama migration backup copies and orphan blobs. Keywords: copias de Ollama, blobs huérfanos, liberar GB.
Read-only, needs no scan. Lists migration backups (Ollama 0.40+ keeps the original copy until `ollama rm`), blobs no manifest references, abandoned partial downloads and backup-looking folders, each with size, owning model and `safe`. Safe means the migrated model's manifest and blobs exist, every manifest is readable and nothing is recent. Returns reclaimable_bytes (safe items only), reasons for the rest, model completeness and whether Ollama is busy.
Sinónimos: copias de seguridad de Ollama, cuánto puedo liberar de Ollama, modelos duplicados tras actualizar.

models_dir.description: Ollama models folder; default OLLAMA_MODELS or ~/.ollama/models

kind.description: Only this kind of item (backups, orphan blobs, partial downloads...)

schema.name: disk_ollama_free
schema.description:
Free Ollama backups and orphans marked safe. Keywords: liberar copias de Ollama, borrar backups.
Frees ONLY items disk_ollama_backups marks safe, re-detected at call time. dry_run=true by default (plan only); a real run needs dry_run=false AND confirm=true, after showing the user the list. Refuses while Ollama has loaded models, is pulling or creating, or the folder cannot be verified. Every call is audited in data/ollama-free-audit.jsonl.
Sinónimos: libera lo que sobra de Ollama, borra las copias de la migración.

ids.description: Item ids from disk_ollama_backups; omit for every safe item

models_dir.description: Ollama models folder; default as disk_ollama_backups

dry_run.description: True (default) only returns the plan, sizes and blockers; nothing changes

confirm.description: Must be true (with dry_run=false) to delete anything. Say so to the user first.

mode.description: 'trash' (default): Recycle Bin, frees disk once emptied. 'permanent': deleted for good. Migration backups are removed with `ollama rm <digest>` (needs the Ollama server running; cannot be undone, downgrading below 0.40 would need a re-pull)

schema.name: disk_zip_plan
schema.description:
Dry-run: plan ZIP parts under a size limit. Keywords: partir en zips, dividir en partes, zip de 990 MB.
Takes a folder and says which files go into part_001.zip, part_002.zip... so every part stays under the limit (upload sites with a per-file cap), with estimated part sizes and the files bigger than the limit. Writes nothing. 'stored' sizes are exact; 'deflated' are upper bounds. Sizes: '990mb' decimal, '990mib' binary, plain bytes. Default excludes: Thumbs.db, desktop.ini, .DS_Store, *.tmp, ~$* (an explicit exclude list replaces them).
Sinónimos: partir esta carpeta en zips, cuántos zips saldrían, zip para subir a una web.

path.description: Absolute folder to split, e.g. D:\Fotos

out_dir.description: Output folder to validate and show; default <path>_zips

limit.description: Maximum size of each ZIP: '990mb', '25mb', '2gb', '990mib' or bytes

margin.description: Safety margin subtracted from the limit

too_large.description: Files that alone exceed the limit: skip, fail, move (to too_large/) or split (raw volumes .zip.001, .002...)

include.description: Only files matching one of these globs, e.g. ['*.jpg']

exclude.description: Skip files or folders matching these globs, e.g. ['*.tmp', 'node_modules']

list_files.description: List every file of every part instead of a short sample

confirm.description: Needed when the source is a whole drive root

schema.name: disk_zip_split
schema.description:
Split a folder into ZIPs under a size limit. Keywords: partir en zips, comprimir por partes, zip de 990 MB.
Creates part_001.zip, part_002.zip... in out_dir (default <folder>_zips, never inside the source), each guaranteed <= limit (checked before adding each file, measured when closed). Keeps folder structure and writes manifest.txt. Output folder must be empty or new unless overwrite=true; refuses drive roots, Windows, Program Files and the profile root. Runs as a job: wait=true blocks and returns every part, wait=false then use disk_zip_status.
Sinónimos: parte esta carpeta en zips, zips de 25 MB para el correo.

path.description: Absolute folder to split, e.g. D:\Fotos

out_dir.description: Output folder; default <path>_zips next to the source

limit.description: Maximum size of each ZIP: '990mb', '25mb', '2gb', '990mib' or bytes

margin.description: Safety margin subtracted from the limit

too_large.description: Files alone bigger than the limit: 'skip' (default), 'fail' (refuse to start), 'split' (own ZIP cut in raw volumes name.zip.001, .002...; open the .001 with 7-Zip or join with `copy /b`) or 'move' (MOVES the original to out_dir/too_large/; needs confirm=true)

include.description: Only files matching one of these globs, e.g. ['*.jpg']

overwrite.description: Replace existing parts with the same prefix (nothing else is touched)

manifest.description: Write manifest.txt in the output folder

confirm.description: Required for too_large='move' (moves user files) and for a whole drive as source

timeout_s.description: Maximum seconds to wait when wait=true (default 150, under an assistant's usual 180 s call limit); past it the job keeps running

schema.name: disk_zip_status
schema.description:
Progress of a ZIP split job. Keywords: estado del zip, progreso, cuánto falta.
Bytes done and total, current file, part number and, when finished, the summary with every part and its real size. Without job it reports the last one.
Sinónimos: cómo va el zip, qué parte lleva, ya ha terminado de comprimir.

job.description: Job id returned by disk_zip_split; omit for the last job

wait_s.description: Wait up to this many seconds for the job to finish before answering

schema.name: disk_zip_cancel
schema.description:
Cancel the running ZIP split job. Keywords: cancelar zip, parar la compresión, detener.
Closed parts stay; the part being written is deleted, so no half-written ZIP is left behind.
Sinónimos: para el zip, cancela la compresión, detén la división en partes.

job.description: Job id; omit for the last job
